findings.title: Store.Load silently discards file-read errors as nil
findings.note: Any read failure (permission, disk, transient IO) is swallowed with no log and no error return; caller gets nil indistinguishable from 'store empty'. The error value is discarded entirely rather than propagated or logged.

findings.title: Store.Load logs unmarshal failure without the cause and returns partial data
findings.note: The printed message never includes err, so the underlying cause is lost. Load still returns the possibly-empty out map as if valid, with no error return path for callers to detect the failure.

findings.title: httpc.Fetch swallows both request and body-read errors, returning empty string
findings.note: Get() failure and ReadAll() failure both collapse to an empty-string return with no logging; the only call site (main.go:28) also discards the return value with '_ =', so a broken health check is completely invisible end to end.

looks_bad_but_fine.why: legacyHandler panics with 'not implemented' rather than swallowing an error; a panic surfaces loudly rather than masking failure, so it is not error-masking even though it looks abrupt.
dispatch.Run's error is checked and passed to log.Fatal, which preserves the cause and halts the process; this is a proper process-boundary handling, not masking.

not_assessed: No claims made about test coverage, CVE/vulnerability status, dependency currency, deprecation policy enforcement, or flakiness for this family; httpc.Fetch is marked Deprecated in-source but no claim is made about whether callers have migrated beyond what grep shows.
